# the mediagraphy.in: full text

Source: https://themediagraphy.in/  |  Updated: 11 November 2026

> Digital marketing and content studio in Kalyan East, Maharashtra, India. We run Google Maps and local SEO, Meta lead campaigns, social media, landing pages, WhatsApp lead routing and on-site video shoots for local businesses in Kalyan, Dombivli, Ulhasnagar, Titwala, Ambernath, Badlapur and Thane. Plans start at Rs 5,999 a month (our fee only); ad spend is paid by the client directly to Google and Meta with no commission.

---

# Services

## Google Maps & Local SEO
URL: https://themediagraphy.in/services/google-maps-local-seo/
Most local customers check Google Maps before they walk in or call. We set up and look after your Google Business Profile, so your shop, clinic or showroom appears with the right photos, timings, services and reviews. No ad spend is needed for this.

Included:
- Claim and verify the profile: We claim your listing or create it, finish Google's verification and fix the basics: name, category, phone, timings and address.
- Services, products and photos: We add your real services, price lists where they help, and 10 or more photos taken at your place, not stock pictures.
- Reviews, the honest way: A QR card for your counter and a short WhatsApp message to ask happy customers for a Google review. We help you reply to every review. We never write fake ones.
- Posts and offers: Regular Google posts for offers, festivals and new arrivals, so the profile never looks abandoned.
- Call, directions and WhatsApp: The call and directions buttons, plus a WhatsApp link through your website or appointment link, set up and tested, so one tap becomes one enquiry.
- Local keywords: The words customers really use, in English, Marathi and Hindi, placed in your profile and website where they belong.
- A monthly report: Views, calls, direction requests and what we will change next month, in plain language.

What to expect: Most profile improvements start to show in 3 to 6 weeks. Where you appear on the map depends on the competition around you, your reviews and how complete your profile is, so we never promise a position.
What we never do: Fake reviews or paid reviews; Fake addresses or virtual offices; A promised ranking or "page one" guarantee
What we need from you: Your business name, logo and phone number; A few photos, if you have them; Access to your Google Business Profile, or the Gmail it was created with
Plans: Included from the Aarambh plan, ₹5,999 a month.

Common mistakes: Keywords in the business name. Adding "best dentist in Kalyan" to the name breaks Google's rules and can get the profile suspended. Two profiles for one shop. A duplicate splits reviews and can get both removed. One real location has one profile. Old timings and phone numbers. Customers who arrive at a closed shop do not return. Festival hours need to be added in advance.
How we measure it: Profile views. How often the profile is shown for searches and on the map. Calls and direction requests. The taps that mean someone intends to visit. We report these each month. Review count and rating. Genuine reviews gained, and whether each was answered.

Q: Do I need to spend on ads for Google Maps?
A: No. Google Maps and local search work is free of ad spend. Your plan fee covers our time to set it up and look after it.

Q: What if someone else already claimed my listing?
A: We help you request ownership through Google's own process. How long that takes is up to Google, and we keep you updated.

Q: How many reviews do I need?
A: There is no magic number. In our free audit we treat a 4.2 star rating with 25 or more reviews as a healthy local benchmark, and we show you how to get there with real customers.


## Meta Lead Campaigns
URL: https://themediagraphy.in/services/meta-lead-campaigns/
We run lead campaigns for businesses in Kalyan, Dombivli, Ulhasnagar, Titwala and Thane. Your ads show to people near you. Interested people leave their number or message you on WhatsApp. You pay Meta directly in rupees, from an ad account in your own name.

Included:
- An ad account in your name: You own the account and the data. We work inside it, and you can see every rupee spent.
- Local targeting: Areas, radius and audiences chosen around where your customers actually live and travel.
- Creative in your customers' language: Ad copy and visuals in Marathi, Hindi or English, built around a clear local offer.
- Lead forms or Click-to-WhatsApp: Short forms that ask only what you need, or ads that open a WhatsApp chat with a ready message.
- Conversions API and Pixel tracking: Tracking that tells Meta which clicks became real enquiries, so the ads learn and you can see the true cost of each enquiry.
- Weekly improvements: We check the numbers every week, pause what is not working and put money behind what is.
- A monthly report: Leads, cost per lead, calls and what changes next, shared on WhatsApp and as a PDF.

What to expect: First enquiries often arrive within 7 to 14 days. Results become steadier by month 2 or 3, after the first round of optimisation. For one shop or clinic we suggest starting with ₹8,000 to ₹15,000 a month in ad spend. Below ₹5,000 the ads rarely get enough data to learn.
What we never do: Take a commission or markup on your ad spend; Promise a fixed number of leads; Buy followers, likes or fake engagement
What we need from you: Your offer, price or package you want to promote; Access to your Facebook page and ad account, or help creating them; Someone who can reply to enquiries quickly, ideally within 15 minutes
Plans: One managed campaign from the Shuru plan, ₹9,999 a month. Meta and Google together from the Vikas plan, ₹19,999 a month. Ad spend is separate.

Common mistakes: A budget too small to learn. Below about ₹5,000 a month the ads rarely get enough results to improve. We say so before you spend. An offer that is not clear. A vague ad brings vague enquiries. One offer, one price or benefit and one next step work better. Slow replies. A lead that waits hours is often gone. Ads cannot fix a reply that never comes.
How we measure it: Cost per enquiry. Ad spend divided by real enquiries, tracked from the ad to the call or chat. Enquiries answered in 15 minutes. Reply speed from your own team, which often decides the result. Customers gained. How many enquiries became customers, as you tell us.

Q: Is the ad budget included in the plan fee?
A: No. Your ad budget is separate and paid by you straight to Meta, from your own account. We take no commission and add no markup.

Q: How soon should I reply to a lead from an ad?
A: Within 15 minutes in working hours if you can. A fast first reply often decides whether the enquiry becomes a visit. We help you set up quick replies so this is realistic.

Q: What is Conversions API?
A: It is a way of sending real enquiry data back to Meta, so the ads learn which clicks turn into customers. Without it, the ads are guessing.


## Social Media Management
URL: https://themediagraphy.in/services/social-media-management/
A page that posts regularly, in the language your customers speak, looks like a business that is open and worth a visit. We plan, design, edit and publish your content, so you can run your business instead of chasing captions.

Included:
- A monthly content plan: Offers, tips, festival greetings and behind-the-scenes posts planned ahead, shared with you before anything goes live.
- Designed posts: Clean, on-brand posts for Instagram and Facebook, in Marathi, Hindi or English.
- Reels with local captions: Short vertical videos edited with captions and text in the local language, made from clips and photos you send or from an on-site visit.
- Festival and season creatives: Diwali, Ganeshotsav, Gudi Padwa, Eid, Navratri and wedding season, ready before the rush.
- Reply support: Guidance and quick-reply templates so comments and DMs are answered the same day.
- A monthly report: What was posted, what people responded to and what we will do next month.

What to expect: Posting regularly builds trust slowly. Social content works best together with Google Maps and a small paid campaign, which is why most plans combine them. Reels and ads need your ad budget to reach more people.
What we never do: Buy followers or likes; Post without your approval of the plan; Use stock photos where a real photo of your shop is possible
What we need from you: Your logo and brand colours, if you have them; Photos and short clips from your phone; A quick yes or change on the monthly plan
Plans: 8 posts a month in the Aarambh plan, ₹5,999. 12 posts and 4 reels a month from the Shuru plan, ₹9,999.

Common mistakes: Posting in bursts. A flurry of posts followed by silence looks abandoned. A rhythm you can keep works better. Generic stock pictures. Local customers can tell. A real photo of your own shop earns more trust. Only English captions. Many customers decide in Marathi or Hindi. The language should match the audience.
How we measure it: Posts and reels delivered. What was planned, approved and published, matched against your plan. Replies and messages. How many comments and messages came in, and how fast they were answered. Enquiries from social. Calls and chats that started from Instagram or Facebook.

Q: Do you post for me, or just make the content?
A: Both. We make the content, share the plan for your approval and publish it on your pages.

Q: Can you create posts in Marathi and Hindi?
A: Yes. Posts, reels, ad copy and WhatsApp messages can be in Marathi, Hindi or English, whichever your customers use.

Q: Do I need to send photos every month?
A: Photos and clips from your phone help a lot. When your plan includes an on-site shoot, we take them ourselves.


## Websites & Landing Pages
URL: https://themediagraphy.in/services/websites-landing-pages/
Most of your customers will open your page on a phone, often on a mobile network. We build light, clear pages with your price, photos, a short form and a WhatsApp button, so a visitor can reach you in one tap.

Included:
- A landing page for one offer: One focused page for your best offer with photos, price, a short form and a WhatsApp button. Your ads send people here instead of to a busy website.
- A full website: A fast, mobile-friendly website for the businesses that need more than one page, with local search work included.
- Call and WhatsApp on every page: A sticky call and WhatsApp button, so visitors never have to hunt for your number.
- Built to load fast on 4G: Compressed images, clean code and no heavy extras, because slow pages lose visitors.
- Tracking you can read: Enquiries from the page are counted, so your report shows what the page is really doing.
- Marathi, Hindi and English: Pages written for the people who will read them.

What to expect: A good landing page changes how many visitors turn into enquiries. It does not create demand by itself, so we pair it with Google Maps or ads. We agree the page and the timeline with you before work begins.
What we never do: Lock your domain or content to us; Add heavy animations that slow the page; Copy another business's page
What we need from you: Your offer, prices and a few real photos; Your logo and brand colours; Your domain name, or we guide you to buy one in your name
Plans: A landing page for your offer is part of the Pragati plan, ₹29,999 a month. A website with local SEO is part of the Shikhar plan, ₹44,999 a month.

Common mistakes: A busy home page for an ad click. Visitors from an ad need one clear offer, not a menu of everything. A landing page keeps them on one path. Heavy images and effects. Slow pages lose people on mobile data. We compress images and keep the code light. No visible phone or WhatsApp button. If the next step is hard to find, visitors leave. A sticky button fixes that.
How we measure it: Visitors who tap call or WhatsApp. The simplest measure of whether the page works. Forms submitted. Counted and shown in your monthly report. Page speed on mobile. Checked on a typical phone and connection before we hand over.

Q: Do I own my domain and my website?
A: Yes. Your domain is bought in your name and your content stays yours.

Q: Will the page work on slow mobile data?
A: That is the point. We build for mobile first and keep the pages light, so they open quickly on 4G.

Q: What is a landing page and why do I need one?
A: It is one web page for one offer, with photos, price, a short form and a WhatsApp button. Ads send people here, so more visitors turn into enquiries.


## WhatsApp Lead Routing
URL: https://themediagraphy.in/services/whatsapp-lead-routing/
For most local customers, WhatsApp is how they ask, compare and book. A slow reply is a lost customer. We set up WhatsApp so enquiries get an instant answer, reach the right person on your team and are followed up until they become a sale or a clear no.

Included:
- WhatsApp Business profile: Business name, hours, address, website and a greeting message set up properly.
- Catalogue: Your products or services with photos and prices, so customers can browse inside WhatsApp.
- Quick replies and auto-replies: Instant answers to common questions, even when you are busy or closed.
- Routing to your team: Enquiries from ads, Google Maps and your website reach the right person with the details attached.
- A lead sheet or CRM: Every enquiry saved with its status, so nobody is forgotten. Small shops start with a shared sheet, bigger teams get a proper CRM.
- Follow-up reminders: Reminders that help your team reply within 15 minutes and follow up again.

What to expect: The tools only help if someone replies. We set up the system and show your team how to use it, and the monthly report shows how many enquiries came in and how many were followed up.
What we never do: Send spam or bulk messages to people who did not ask; Use bots that pretend to be a person; Share your customer list with anyone
What we need from you: The phone number you want to use for business WhatsApp; Your product or service list and prices; The people on your team who will reply
Plans: WhatsApp Business set-up from the Shuru plan, ₹9,999 a month. Catalogue and auto-replies from the Vikas plan, ₹19,999. Automation and CRM set-up in the Shikhar plan, ₹44,999.

Common mistakes: No away message. A chat sent at night with no reply sets a bad first impression. An away message sets expectations. One person holding every chat. If that person is busy, enquiries wait. Labels and routing share the load. Bulk messages to people who did not ask. It breaks WhatsApp's rules, and it annoys customers. We do not do it.
How we measure it: Enquiries received and labelled. How many chats came in and what status each reached. Reply time. Whether your team met the 15-minute target in working hours. Follow-ups done. How many quiet enquiries got a second message.

Q: Do I need the WhatsApp API?
A: Most small businesses start with the free WhatsApp Business app. We suggest the API only when you have a team and enough enquiries to need it.

Q: What happens when I get many enquiries at once?
A: Labels, quick replies and a simple routing rule share the load across your team, so each enquiry gets a first answer quickly. We set this up with you and show your staff how to use it.

Q: Can ads open a WhatsApp chat directly?
A: Yes. Click-to-WhatsApp ads open a chat with a ready message, which is how many local customers like to enquire.


## On-Site Video Shoots
URL: https://themediagraphy.in/services/on-site-video-shoots/
A real photo of your own street, your own shop front and your own team builds more trust than any stock image. Our team visits you, records photos and many clips in one visit, and turns them into reels, posts and ad creatives for the month.

Included:
- A short plan before we come: A simple shot list so the visit is quick and we capture what you actually sell.
- On-site photos and clips: Your shop front, your products, your team and your customers, with permission, in one visit.
- Edited reels with local captions: Short vertical videos with captions and text in Marathi, Hindi or English.
- Posts and ad creatives: The same shoot is cut into posts and ads, so one visit feeds the whole month.
- Clear delivery: Files delivered in the formats you need. We agree the turnaround before the shoot.

What to expect: One shoot gives you enough material for several reels, posts and ads. We schedule shoots in advance, so plan them around your quiet hours. We film customers or patients only with their permission.
What we never do: Film customers or patients without permission; Use stock footage and call it your shop; Keep your raw files from you
What we need from you: A suitable time, ideally when the shop is quiet; Anything you want featured: products, offers, team; A person on site who can say yes to the shot list
Plans: One on-site shoot a month in the Pragati plan, ₹29,999. Two a month in the Shikhar plan, ₹44,999.

Common mistakes: Shooting at the busiest hour. A noisy rush makes footage hard to use and annoys customers. We plan around your quiet hours. No shot list. Without a plan we film everything and use little. A short list before the visit saves time. Filming people without asking. We film customers and patients only with their permission.
How we measure it: Material delivered. The reels, posts and ad creatives cut from each shoot. Turnaround. Agreed before the shoot, and shown in your plan. Use in ads and posts. Which clips were used and how they performed in the monthly report.

Q: How long does a shoot take?
A: It depends on your shop and the shot list. We agree the length, the date and the turnaround with you before we come, and we plan the visit for your quiet hours.

Q: Do you travel to my shop?
A: Yes. We come to your shop, clinic or site anywhere in Kalyan, Dombivli, Ulhasnagar, Titwala and nearby.

Q: Can I get the shoot without a full plan?
A: Ask us on WhatsApp. We will tell you honestly what makes sense for your business and budget.


# Plans

## Aarambh (Rs 5,999 a month)
We make your shop easy to find on Google Maps and keep your Instagram and Facebook active.
Includes: Google Business Profile set-up and care; 8 social posts a month; Review and reply support; Simple monthly report (WhatsApp / PDF)
Good fit if: You have one shop, a small budget, and you want to start showing up when people search "near me".
Maybe not if: You want paid ads to bring enquiries quickly. Look at Shuru or Vikas instead.
Suggested ad spend (paid by the client to Google and Meta): Rs 3,000–8,000

## Shuru (Rs 9,999 a month)
Everything in Aarambh, plus more content, short videos and your first paid ad campaign.
Includes: Everything in Aarambh; 12 posts + 4 reels a month; 1 Meta lead campaign; WhatsApp Business set-up; Monthly report and call
Good fit if: You want regular posts and videos, and you are ready to try paid ads for the first time.
Maybe not if: You want ads on Google as well, or someone checking your numbers every two weeks. Look at Vikas.
Suggested ad spend (paid by the client to Google and Meta): Rs 8,000–15,000

## Vikas (Rs 19,999 a month)
Everything in Shuru, plus Google ads, proper tracking of every enquiry, and a call every two weeks.
Includes: Everything in Shuru; Meta + Google ads management; WhatsApp catalogue and auto-replies; Lead tracking (Pixel / CAPI); Fortnightly strategy call
Good fit if: You want enquiries coming in steadily and you want to know which ads actually bring them.
Maybe not if: You also want a dedicated landing page and a monthly shoot at your shop. Look at Pragati.
Suggested ad spend (paid by the client to Google and Meta): Rs 15,000–30,000

## Pragati (Rs 29,999 a month)
Everything in Vikas, plus a special page for your best offer, a monthly shoot at your place, and a weekly call.
Includes: Everything in Vikas; A landing page for your offer; 1 on-site shoot a month; Weekly strategy call; Lead tracking sheet with reminders
Good fit if: You are growing, you have a clear offer to push, and you want fresh photos and videos every month.
Maybe not if: You need a full website, several services promoted together, or a dedicated manager. Look at Shikhar.
Suggested ad spend (paid by the client to Google and Meta): Rs 30,000–60,000

## Shikhar (Rs 44,999 a month)
Everything in Pragati, plus a full website, two shoots a month, one person who manages your account, and automatic WhatsApp follow-ups.
Includes: Everything in Pragati; Website + local SEO; 2 on-site shoots a month; Dedicated campaign manager; WhatsApp automation and CRM set-up
Good fit if: You have several services or a team, and you want one partner to run the whole system from ads to follow-up.
Maybe not if: You are just starting or have one small shop. A smaller plan will give you better value.
Suggested ad spend (paid by the client to Google and Meta): Rs 60,000 and above

# Areas

## Kalyan
URL: https://themediagraphy.in/areas/kalyan/
Our studio is in Kalyan East, so Kalyan is where we can reach your door most easily. We work with shops, clinics, classes and builders on both sides of the station, and we start by walking the street your customers walk.

- Studio base: Kalyan East
- Railway: Kalyan Junction, where the Central Railway main line splits towards Kasara and towards Karjat
- Two sides: Kalyan East and Kalyan West, divided by the station and the tracks
- Languages heard: Marathi and Hindi most, with English for ads and professional services

Two sides of one station. Many Kalyan customers think in terms of East or West before they think of a road. In the West, the older market streets sit close to the station. In the East, there are more residential colonies and newer housing towards Kalyan-Shil Road. A Google profile, an ad radius and a shop board that name the right side and the right landmark save a customer a wrong turn.
Station-first directions. People here often give directions from the station, a chowk or a well-known shop. We write your Google profile description, your ad copy and your WhatsApp greeting using the landmark your own customers use, and we check it against the real street before it goes live.
Where we are quickest. Because we are based in Kalyan East, first meetings, audit visits and shoots here are the easiest for us to plan. We agree dates ahead on WhatsApp so we never turn up at your busiest hour.

Example searches: dentist near Chinchpada Kalyan East; gym in Kolsewadi; jeweller near Kalyan station; tuition classes Kalyan West; salon near Khadakpada; 2 BHK flats Kalyan-Shil Road

Local calendar: Navratri: Festive shopping and a lot of footfall near the old market streets. Offers need to be ready weeks before. Diwali and wedding season: Jewellers, boutiques, salons and photographers see the most enquiries. Start earlier than you think. Admission months: Classes and schools get their enquiries in a short window, so lead forms and replies need to be ready first.

We are based in Kalyan East. For shops in Kalyan East and West and along Kalyan-Shil Road, we visit for the first meeting, the audit and any shoot, with dates agreed in advance on WhatsApp.

Q: Should I target Kalyan East and Kalyan West separately?
A: Often yes. Customers on each side behave like two neighbourhoods. We set the ad radius and the profile wording around the side your customers come from, and widen it only when your own numbers show people travelling across.

Q: Which parts of Kalyan do you visit?
A: We visit shops across Kalyan East, Kalyan West and along Kalyan-Shil Road. We plan visits in advance so they fit around your quiet hours.

Q: Can one campaign cover Kalyan and Dombivli together?
A: It can, but a shop usually draws from one side of one town. We start with a tight area around you and add Dombivli only if your enquiries show people coming from there.


## Dombivli
URL: https://themediagraphy.in/areas/dombivli/
Dombivli customers know their town by its roads. Phadke Road, Tilak Road and Manpada Road in the East, Gupte Road and Deendayal Road in the West. We build your Google profile, ad area and wording around those names.

- Railway: Dombivli station on the Central Railway main line, between Thane and Kalyan
- Two sides: Dombivli East and Dombivli West, either side of the station
- Nearby stations: Kopar towards Thane and Thakurli towards Kalyan
- Languages heard: Marathi in daily life for many households, with Hindi and English in business

Road names do the work. A line such as "near Phadke Road" in Marathi sounds different from a generic city ad in English. Our creative comparison on the home page shows that difference side by side, and Dombivli is where it matters most because customers here often search with the road name.
One shop, one profile. Dombivli East and Dombivli West are different catchments. A shop should have one Google profile for its real location, not one for each side. We make sure the pin, the address and the service area all say the same thing.
Business neighbours. Alongside everyday shops and clinics, Dombivli East has an industrial estate. Businesses there often sell to other businesses, so Google search and WhatsApp matter more than Instagram. The free audit tells us which side of the mix you need.

Example searches: dentist near Phadke Road Dombivli; classes near Manpada Road; salon Dombivli West Deendayal Road; pharmacy near Dombivli station; gym in Sonarpada; interior designer Dombivli

Local calendar: Gudi Padwa: A major local moment. Greetings, offers and shop-front content in Marathi land well when planned before the day. Ganeshotsav: Strong footfall and festive spending. Decor, sweets, clothing and gifting see it first. Diwali and wedding season: Jewellers, boutiques, photographers and caterers: plan shoots and ads at least a few weeks ahead.

We come to your shop in Dombivli East or West for the first meeting, the audit and any shoot. We plan the visit ahead on WhatsApp so it fits your quiet hours.

Q: Do Dombivli East and West need separate Google profiles?
A: No. A Google profile belongs to one real location. If you have a shop on one side of the station, you have one profile there. A second profile is only for a second real branch.

Q: Do you work with businesses in the Dombivli industrial area?
A: Yes. Those businesses often sell to other businesses, so we lean on Google search, a clear website page and WhatsApp rather than Instagram. We confirm the right mix in the free audit.

Q: Should my ad name the road or just say Dombivli?
A: Often the road or the landmark works better, because it tells the customer you are close. We test both wordings and keep the one your own enquiries prefer.


## Ulhasnagar
URL: https://themediagraphy.in/areas/ulhasnagar/
Ulhasnagar is a market town where customers compare quickly, shop by the camp and chowk, and move between Hindi, Marathi, Sindhi and English in one conversation. We set up your profile, ads and replies to match.

- Railway: Ulhasnagar station on the Central Railway line between Kalyan and Ambernath
- Layout: Divided into numbered camps, from Camp 1 to Camp 5, each with its own chowk and lanes
- Known for: Busy market lanes, with clothing and furniture among the trades people travel here for
- Languages heard: Hindi, Marathi and Sindhi are all in daily use, along with English

The camp is the address. Ulhasnagar's camp numbers work like neighbourhood names. A Google profile that gets the camp, the chowk and the nearest well-known shop right is easier to find and easier to reach. Wrong or missing camp details are the most common reason customers cannot find a shop here.
A mixed-language market. Hindi, Marathi and English are all useful, and Sindhi is part of everyday life. We test which language works best for each offer, and we ask you or your team to supply any Sindhi wording so that it is right.
Compare-first customers. Customers here often compare prices at two or three shops before they buy. A clear offer, a real photo of your shop and a fast WhatsApp reply do more than a large ad budget, and that is where we begin.

Example searches: mobile shop Ulhasnagar Camp 3; furniture showroom Ulhasnagar; lehenga shop Ulhasnagar; coaching classes Ulhasnagar Camp 4; salon near Ulhasnagar station; electrician Ulhasnagar

Local calendar: Cheti Chand: The Sindhi new year, a big day for greetings, offers and gifting. Content in the right language and tone is appreciated. Diwali and wedding season: Clothing, furniture, electronics and jewellery shops see the biggest rush. Photos and catalogues need to be ready first. Month-end and festival sales: Price-aware customers respond to a clear offer with an end date, shown on the shop board and in WhatsApp status.

We come to your shop in Ulhasnagar for the first meeting, the audit and any shoot. We plan the visit ahead so it fits around your busy hours.

Q: Do you write ads in Sindhi?
A: Our core languages are Marathi, Hindi and English. For Sindhi lines, such as a festival greeting, we ask you or your team to give us the wording so it is correct, and we design the post around it.

Q: How do I stand out when many shops nearby sell the same thing?
A: Show something the next shop cannot: your real shop front, a clear price or offer, a fast reply and genuine reviews. We build those four things before we spend on ads.

Q: Does the camp number matter on my Google profile?
A: Yes. Write the address exactly as customers and the post office know it, including the camp, and keep it the same everywhere online. A mismatch is a common reason a profile is hard to find.


## Titwala
URL: https://themediagraphy.in/areas/titwala/
Titwala is a growing town on the Kasara line, known across the region for its Ganpati temple. Many customers still find a shop by walking past it. We make sure they can also find you on Google Maps, Instagram and WhatsApp.

- Railway: Titwala station on the Central Railway Kasara line, beyond Kalyan, Shahad and Ambivli
- Known for: The Mahaganapati temple, which draws visitors from across the region
- Growth: Newer housing complexes have come up in and around the town, bringing new residents who do not yet know the local shops
- Languages heard: Marathi mostly, with Hindi and English alongside

Newcomers search first. Residents who have just moved into a new complex do not yet know which clinic, tuition class or grocer to trust. They search on Google Maps and ask in housing WhatsApp groups. A complete profile with real photos and reviews is how you are chosen before they ever walk in.
Temple-day footfall. Visitors to the temple pass through on festival days and weekends. Food, sweets, gifts, clothing and travel services can reach them with a clear Google profile that shows timings and a call or directions button.
Start small, start local. Our estimates treat Titwala as a lower-cost ad market, so a modest budget can go further. A strong Maps profile can do much of the work without any ad spend, and ads can be added once enquiries are ready to be handled.

Example searches: clinic near Titwala station; tuition classes Titwala; flats in Titwala; sweet shop near Titwala Ganpati temple; salon Titwala; grocery home delivery Titwala

Local calendar: Ganeshotsav and temple festivals: The busiest period for footfall. Timings, offers and directions on Google should be correct before it begins. Admission months: Parents compare schools and classes quickly. Open-day bookings on WhatsApp work best when the reply is immediate. Move-in seasons: New residents settle in around housing handovers. Welcome offers for new neighbours can bring a first visit.

We are based in Kalyan East and come to Titwala for meetings and shoots. We plan these ahead on WhatsApp.

Q: Is a smaller budget enough in Titwala?
A: Often, yes. Start from the audit and the estimator, and we will tell you honestly whether a smaller budget is better spent on Google Maps and WhatsApp first.

Q: Can a shop near the temple reach visitors on Google?
A: Yes. A complete profile with correct timings, photos and a directions button helps visitors who search on their phone while they are nearby. Festival-day hours should be added in advance.

Q: How do I reach new residents in the housing complexes?
A: Through Google Maps, a short welcome offer and a quick WhatsApp reply. Local housing groups are where recommendations spread, so happy customers and genuine reviews matter most.

URL: https://themediagraphy.in/areas/thane/
Thane is a bigger and more crowded market than the KDMC towns. Many businesses bid for the same people, so tight area targeting, a sharp offer and fast replies matter more. We plan around your exact catchment so the budget is not wasted.

- Railway: Thane station on the Central Railway main line, the first big stop before the Kalyan and Dombivli belt
- Local character: Often called the city of lakes, with a mix of old market areas and newer towers

Catchment, not city. Thane is large enough that a shop in Majiwada and a shop in Kopri draw from different pools. We draw the ad area around where your customers live and travel, which is usually a few neighbourhoods, not the whole city.
Cost per enquiry runs higher. Our estimator assumes a higher cost per enquiry for Thane than for the rest of the belt, because more businesses compete for the same people. We would rather show a cautious range than a hopeful one, and we tell you early if a smaller budget is better spent on Maps and WhatsApp.
Google and Meta together. In a competitive market, being found when someone searches on Google and being seen on Instagram both help. The Vikas plan manages both, with tracking so you can see which one is paying for itself.

Example searches: dentist near Gokhale Road Thane; gym on Ghodbunder Road; salon Naupada Thane; interior designer Thane West; 2 BHK flats Majiwada; yoga classes Vartak Nagar

Admission and exam months: Classes and schools compete hard. A clear fee page and an instant WhatsApp reply decide the enquiry. Real-estate launches: Project launches need MahaRERA details in the ad, a walkthrough video and a fast site-visit follow-up.

We are based in Kalyan East. We serve Thane clients through calls, WhatsApp and visits that we plan ahead, so we can reach you without pretending to be around the corner.

Q: Why are ads more expensive in Thane?
A: More businesses bid for the same people, so each click and each enquiry costs more. That is why we focus on a tight area, a strong offer and fast replies rather than a bigger budget.

Q: Do you serve Thane from Kalyan?
A: Yes. We are based in Kalyan East. Most of the work happens through calls, WhatsApp and shared reports, and we visit for meetings and shoots that we plan in advance.

Q: Can you advertise a real estate project in Thane?

Ambernath and Badlapur are two separate towns on the Karjat line, beyond Ulhasnagar. Customers in each compare nearby options quickly and travel to the next town only when they must. We help you be the first option they see.

Two towns, two catchments. A customer in Badlapur seldom shops in Ambernath. We plan one profile, one ad radius and one set of landmarks for each town, rather than treating the stretch as a single market.
A practical way to begin. Our estimates treat this belt as a lower-cost ad market. Many shops here can start with the Aarambh or Shuru plan and add ads when enquiries are ready to be handled, which keeps early spend small.
Commuter households. Many residents travel to Kalyan, Thane or Mumbai for work, which means they search and message in the evening and on weekends. Posting, offers and replies timed for those hours reach them when they are free to act.

Q: How far should the ad radius reach?

# Guides

## How to set up a Google Business Profile for a shop in Kalyan
URL: https://themediagraphy.in/guides/google-business-profile-setup-kalyan/
Short answer: Search for your business on Google Maps, claim it or add it, choose the right categories, add your real address or service area, timings, phone number and photos, then complete Google's verification. Keep the name, address and phone identical everywhere online. Free, and the base of every local marketing plan.

### Before you start
Gather four things so you can finish in one sitting.
- The business name exactly as it appears on your shop board.
- The address as customers and the post office write it, including the camp, wing or floor.
- A phone number you answer, and a Gmail account that you control.
- Five to ten real photos taken at your place: the front of the shop, the inside, your team and your best products or services.

### Step 1: find it or add it
Open Google Maps on your phone, search for your business name and your area. If a listing already exists, choose to claim it. If not, add the business. Do not create a second listing for the same shop, because duplicates split your reviews and can get both removed.

### Step 2: name, category and details
Use your real-world name. Do not add keywords or an area to the name, because Google's guidelines do not allow it and it can get the profile suspended. Choose one main category that describes what you are, such as Dentist or Jewellery store, then add a few secondary categories that are also true. Add your timings, including special hours for festivals, your phone number and a website or WhatsApp link if you have one.

### Step 3: address or service area
If customers visit you, show your address and put the pin exactly on your entrance. If you travel to customers and do not receive visitors, you can hide the address and list the areas you serve. Never use a fake address, a friend's shop or a virtual office. That is the quickest way to lose a profile.

### Step 4: verification
Google decides how to verify you. It may ask for a short video of your shop front and signage, a phone call, an email or a code. The time it takes varies, and it can ask for more proof. Follow the steps in the app and answer promptly. If you are asked for a video, film a slow walk from the street into the shop, showing the board, the counter and something that proves you run the business.

### Step 5: make it complete
A complete profile looks cared for.
- Add your services, with a line or two about each, and prices where they help.
- Upload real photos, and add new ones every month.
- Write a short description of what you do and where, in plain words.
- Share offers and updates as Google posts.
- Reply to every review, kindly, within a couple of days.

### Keep your details the same everywhere
Your name, address and phone number should read the same on your website, Instagram, Facebook and any business directory. Small differences confuse both customers and search engines. Decide on one version and copy it exactly.

### What to expect
Google decides who appears first for a search, based mainly on how relevant your profile is, how far you are from the person searching, and how well known you are. Nobody can pay for a position or promise one. A complete profile with real photos and genuine reviews gives you the best chance, and improvements usually build over weeks, not days.

Q: Is a Google Business Profile free?
A: Yes. Creating and managing the profile costs nothing. You pay only if you choose to run Google ads separately.

Q: Can I add my WhatsApp number?
A: You can add it to your description or website link. The profile's main call button uses your phone number, so use a number you answer.

Q: What if someone else has already claimed my listing?
A: Use the option to request ownership. Google handles the process and the time it takes is up to Google. We can guide you through it.


## How much should a local shop spend on Instagram and Facebook ads?
URL: https://themediagraphy.in/guides/meta-ads-budget-for-local-shop/
Short answer: Work backwards from the customers you want. Divide the customers you need by the share of enquiries you usually close to get the enquiries you need, then multiply by what one enquiry costs. Start with a small test, read the real cost per enquiry, and then decide. We suggest ₹8,000 to 15,000 a month for one shop.

### Start from customers, not from a budget
Most owners pick an amount and hope. A better method has four short steps.
- Decide how many new customers a month would make the ads worthwhile.
- Estimate what share of enquiries you turn into customers. If you are not sure, use your last ten enquiries to count.
- Divide: customers wanted divided by that share gives the enquiries you need.
- Multiply the enquiries by the cost of one enquiry, which you learn from a small test.

### An example with made-up numbers
Suppose a salon wants 12 new customers a month and turns about one in three enquiries into a booking. That means about 36 enquiries a month. If the first two weeks of ads show that an enquiry costs about ₹150, the monthly ad budget would be about ₹5,400. These figures are invented to show the method. Your own numbers will be different, and they will change by season and area.

### Why a very small budget struggles
Ads learn from results. With a very small budget there are too few enquiries for the system to learn which people respond, so costs stay high and results swing from day to day. That is why we say that below ₹5,000 a month, ads rarely get enough data to learn. If that is your budget, put it into Google Maps, reviews and WhatsApp first.

### What the plan fee is not
Your ad budget is separate from our fee. You pay it straight to Meta and Google, from your own account. We take no commission and add no markup, and you can see every rupee in your own Ads Manager.

### Test, read, then decide
Run a small test for two weeks with a clear offer and a quick-reply WhatsApp or short form. Then look at three things.
- The cost of one enquiry.
- How many enquiries your team actually answered within 15 minutes.
- How many became customers. If enquiries are cheap but few become customers, the fix is usually the offer or the follow-up, not a bigger budget.

### When to raise the budget
Raise it when three things are true: the cost per enquiry is steady, your team can reply fast to more enquiries, and the customers you gain are profitable. Raise it in steps, not all at once, so the ads have time to settle.

Q: Is ₹8,000 a month enough for one shop?
A: For many single shops it is a reasonable place to start a test, together with a good Google profile and fast WhatsApp replies. The right amount depends on your area, offer and how fast you can answer.

Q: Do you take a share of my ad budget?
A: No. You pay Meta and Google directly. Our fee is separate, and there is no commission on ad spend.

Q: Can I use the estimator to plan a budget?
A: Yes. The lead estimator on our tools page gives an illustrative range from typical local figures. Treat it as a guide and replace its assumptions with your own numbers.


## Google Maps or Instagram first? Where to put your first ₹10,000
URL: https://themediagraphy.in/guides/google-maps-or-instagram-first/
Short answer: If customers search when they need you, such as for a dentist, mechanic or pharmacy, start with Google Maps. If they buy by look or mood, such as for a salon, boutique, café or gym, start with Instagram. Many shops do best with a complete Google profile first, because it needs no ad spend.

### Ask how your customers decide
The question is not which platform is better. It is where your customer is when they choose.
- They need something now. A leaking tap, a toothache, a flat tyre. They search on Google and pick from the map.
- They browse and fall in love. A bridal blouse, a haircut idea, a gym transformation. They scroll Instagram and message the shop that looks right.

### Start with Google Maps if
- People say "near me" when they look for you.
- You have a fixed shop, clinic or workshop with an address.
- Your competitors have few photos or reviews.
- You want results that do not need ad spend. The first month's work is a complete profile, real photos, correct timings, a review habit and a way to reply on WhatsApp.

### Start with Instagram if
- Your product looks good on a phone, such as food, fashion, jewellery or interiors.
- You can show real work every week.
- Customers often ask your price or availability in a message. The first month's work is a content plan, a few reels shot at your shop, and a WhatsApp reply that is fast and friendly.

### How to split your first ₹10,000
There is no fixed formula, because ad spend and our fee are separate. As a starting idea, if you have ₹10,000 a month of ad spend and nothing in place, spend little or none on ads for the first few weeks. Fix the Google profile and WhatsApp reply first, because they cost time rather than money. Then put the ad money behind whichever channel is already bringing real enquiries.

### Do not skip the follow-up
Both channels fail if nobody replies. A slow answer loses an enquiry on either platform. Before spending more on either, make sure someone can answer within 15 minutes during opening hours.

Q: Can I do both at once?
A: Yes, and most plans do. The question is only which to build first when time or money is tight.

Q: Which gets results faster?
A: Meta ads can bring first enquiries in a week or two once the offer and replies are ready. Google Maps work usually shows over several weeks. Neither is guaranteed.

Q: What if I do not know how my customers decide?
A: Ask your last ten customers how they found you, and run our free audit. Both will show which channel to build first.


## How to get more Google reviews without breaking Google's rules
URL: https://themediagraphy.in/guides/get-google-reviews-the-right-way/
Short answer: Ask every happy customer, right after good service, with a QR card at the counter and a short WhatsApp message that links straight to your review page. Do not offer gifts or discounts in exchange for reviews, do not ask only happy customers to review, and never buy or write reviews yourself.

### Why reviews matter
Customers read reviews before they walk in or call. Google also treats the number, quality and freshness of reviews as part of how well known a business is. A steady flow of real reviews matters more than a burst of them.

### Ask at the right moment
The best time is just after a good experience: when the bill is paid, the treatment is finished, or the order is delivered. Ask politely and make it effortless.
- Put a QR card at the counter that opens your review page.
- Send a short WhatsApp message with your review link after the visit.
- Ask in the customer's language, whether Marathi, Hindi or English.

### A message you can copy
Hello, thank you for visiting us today. If you were happy with the service, would you mind leaving a short Google review? It takes a minute and helps others nearby find us. Here is the link. Thank you! Keep it short and never pressure anyone.

### What breaks the rules
Google's policies do not allow these, and reviews can be removed or the profile penalised.
- Offering gifts, discounts or money in exchange for reviews.
- Asking only happy customers to review, or sending unhappy ones elsewhere.
- Writing reviews yourself, or having staff and family write them.
- Buying reviews from anyone, at any price.
- Reviewing a competitor.

### How to reply to a bad review
Reply in public, within a day or two, politely and briefly. Thank the person, apologise for the experience without arguing, and offer to fix it offline with a phone number or email. Future customers read your reply as much as the review itself. If a review is spam, fake or off-topic, you can flag it to Google, and Google decides whether to remove it. Honest negative reviews cannot be removed.

### Make it a habit
Decide who asks, when, and how. A counter card, a staff reminder and a WhatsApp template are enough. Reviewing a little every week beats a big push once a year.

Q: Can I give a small discount for a review?
A: No. Offering anything in exchange for a review breaks Google's rules, even when the review is honest.

Q: Can you remove a bad review for me?
A: We can flag reviews that break Google's policies. Google makes the final call. We cannot remove honest negative reviews.

Q: How many reviews do I need?
A: There is no magic number. In our audit we treat 4.2 stars with 25 or more reviews as a healthy local benchmark and show you how to get there with real customers.


## A simple WhatsApp reply system that stops you losing enquiries
URL: https://themediagraphy.in/guides/whatsapp-reply-system-for-leads/
Short answer: Use WhatsApp Business with a greeting message, a handful of quick replies and labels for each enquiry's status. Aim to answer within 15 minutes in working hours, write down who replies when, and follow up once the next day. Speed and a clear next step win local customers.

### Why speed matters
Local customers often message two or three shops at once. The one that answers first, clearly, usually gets the visit. An enquiry that waits half a day is often gone.

### Set up the WhatsApp Business app
The free WhatsApp Business app is enough for most small shops. Set up these pieces.
- A business profile with your name, address, hours and website.
- A greeting message that welcomes new chats.
- An away message for after hours that says when you will reply.
- A catalogue of your products or services with photos and prices.
- Quick replies for the questions you get every day.

### Write your quick replies once
Save answers to the top questions so a reply takes seconds.
- Where are you and what are your timings?
- What is the price or range for this service?
- Can I book a slot today?
- Do you have this in stock? Keep each reply short, friendly and in the customer's language. End each with a clear next step, such as a time or a question.

### Use labels to track status
Give each chat a label such as New, Replied, Visit booked, Done or Lost. At the end of the day, open the New and Replied chats and make sure nobody was forgotten. This single habit stops most lost enquiries.

### The 15-minute rule
Decide who answers and when. During working hours, aim to reply within 15 minutes, even if the reply is only a short acknowledgement and a promise of the full answer. Outside hours, the away message sets expectations. Write down the rule so staff follow it on busy days.

### Follow up once
If a customer goes quiet, send one polite follow-up the next day and one more a few days later, then stop. Never send bulk messages to people who did not ask for them, and let anyone opt out of broadcast messages.

Q: Do I need the WhatsApp Business API?
A: Most small shops do not. The free app is enough until you have a team and a large number of enquiries. We set up the API only when it makes sense.

Q: Can ads open a WhatsApp chat directly?
A: Yes. Click-to-WhatsApp ads open a chat with a ready message. They work best when someone is ready to reply quickly.

Q: Should I use a bot to answer?
A: Auto-replies and saved answers are fine. Do not use a bot that pretends to be a person, and make sure a real person follows up soon.


## Meta lead form ads or click-to-WhatsApp ads: which should you use?
URL: https://themediagraphy.in/guides/meta-lead-ads-vs-click-to-whatsapp/
Short answer: Use lead form ads when you want a name and phone number you can call back, and your team can call quickly. Use click-to-WhatsApp ads when customers prefer to chat first and you can reply fast. Many local businesses start with WhatsApp because it feels natural, then add forms for higher-value offers.

### How lead form ads work
A person taps your ad and a short form opens inside Instagram or Facebook, often with their name and phone number already filled in. They submit it with a tap. The enquiry lands in your account, and you call or message them.

### How click-to-WhatsApp ads work
The ad has a button that opens a WhatsApp chat with your business, often with a ready first message. The customer starts a conversation instead of filling in a form.

### Where lead forms are strong
- You want to qualify people, for example by asking a flat size, a budget or a class level.
- Your team likes to call back.
- The offer is higher value, such as property, interiors or admissions. The risk is lower-quality enquiries, because a form is easy to submit by mistake. Short questions that filter out casual taps help.

### Where click-to-WhatsApp is strong
- Customers like to ask questions before booking.
- You sell products or services with quick answers: a salon slot, a menu, a price.
- You can reply in minutes in Marathi, Hindi or English. The risk is slow replies. A chat that waits goes cold faster than a form.

### A simple way to choose
Ask three questions. Do customers usually message or call first? How fast can we reply? Do we need to filter enquiries before spending time? Messaging-first and fast replies point to WhatsApp. Filtering and call-back habits point to forms. Both can be tested with the same budget, and the cost per real customer, not the cost per tap, decides the winner.

### Whichever you choose, track it
Count every enquiry from the ad to the customer. Tracking set up with Meta's Pixel and Conversions API helps the ads learn which clicks become real enquiries, and shows you the true cost of each one.

Q: Which one is cheaper?
A: It varies by business and area. Compare the cost per real customer, not the cost per tap or form.

Q: Can I run both at the same time?
A: Yes. A small test of each with the same offer usually shows which suits your customers better.

Q: Do I need a website?
A: No. Both formats work without one, which makes them a good start for a small shop. A landing page helps once you want to send people to a detailed offer.


## Marathi, Hindi or English: which language should your ads use?
URL: https://themediagraphy.in/guides/marathi-hindi-english-ad-language/
Short answer: Use the language your customers speak when they decide. In much of Kalyan and Dombivli that is often Marathi, Hindi works across the belt, and English suits professional services and younger audiences. Do not guess: run the same offer in two languages, and let your own enquiries pick the winner.

### Language is part of trust
A customer who reads a line in the language they think in feels it was written for them. The same message in stiff English can feel like it came from far away. For a neighbourhood shop, that difference matters.

### A starting point by audience
These are starting guesses, not rules. Your own enquiries will correct them.
- Marathi: neighbourhood shops, clinics, festivals and family services in areas where Marathi is the main language at home.
- Hindi: the wider belt, mixed neighbourhoods and markets such as Ulhasnagar, and younger audiences who read Hindi comfortably.
- English: professional services, premium products, and audiences that read English first.
- Mixed: short English words inside a Marathi or Hindi line, as people really speak, often reads naturally.

### Write it the way people speak
Avoid textbook translations. A friendly, spoken line beats formal language. Have a native speaker from your own team or family read the copy before it goes live, and use the local landmark or road name that customers use.

### How to test it
Run the same offer and photo in two languages, with the same budget and area, for a couple of weeks. Compare the cost of a real enquiry and how many turn into customers. Keep the winner, then test a new line against it. Small tests teach faster than opinions.

### Do not forget the reply
If the ad is in Marathi, the first WhatsApp reply should be in Marathi too. A mismatch between the ad and the reply loses people. Save quick replies in each language you use.

Q: Do you write in Marathi and Hindi?
A: Yes. Posts, reels, ad copy and WhatsApp messages can be in Marathi, Hindi or English.

Q: What about Sindhi or other languages?
A: Our core languages are Marathi, Hindi and English. For lines in other languages, we ask you for the wording so it is right.

Q: Does Google care what language my profile uses?
A: Write your profile in the language your customers search in. Many shops add a short line in a second language. Keep the name, address and phone identical.


## A local SEO checklist for shops, clinics and classes
URL: https://themediagraphy.in/guides/local-seo-checklist-for-shops/
Short answer: Claim and complete your Google Business Profile, keep your name, address and phone identical everywhere, add real photos, collect genuine reviews, give your website a clear page for each service and area, and add fresh updates monthly. Local search rewards completeness, consistency and real activity, not tricks.

### Google Business Profile
- Claimed, verified and complete, with the right main category.
- Timings, phone number, website or WhatsApp link and services filled in.
- At least ten real photos, with new ones added every month.
- Offers and updates posted regularly.
- Every review answered.

### Name, address and phone
- Written the same way on Google, your website, Instagram, Facebook and any directory.
- No keywords or area stuffed into the business name.
- One profile per real location.

### Reviews
- A QR card at the counter and a WhatsApp message to ask happy customers.
- No gifts, no discounts for reviews, no fake ones.
- Replies that are polite and brief.

### Your website
- A fast page on mobile, with a call and WhatsApp button.
- A clear page for each service you sell and for each area you serve, written for people, not search engines.
- Your address, timings and a map link, matching your Google profile.
- Plain headings and short answers to the questions customers ask.

### Local signals
- The areas, roads and landmarks customers use, in the languages they speak.
- Links or mentions from real local sources, such as a local association or a supplier's page.
- A few trusted business directories with correct details. Quality beats quantity.

### Every month
- Add new photos and one or two updates.
- Check for new reviews and reply.
- Review calls, direction requests and website taps.
- Fix anything that changed: timings, phone numbers, services.
- Write down what you will change next month.

### What not to do
- Do not buy backlinks, reviews or a packaged ranking promise.
- Do not create duplicate profiles or fake addresses.
- Do not copy another business's text word for word.

Q: How long does local SEO take?
A: Improvements to a Google profile usually start to show in several weeks, and keep building. No honest provider can promise a position.

Q: Do I need a website for local SEO?
A: You can start with only a profile. A fast mobile page with a WhatsApp button helps convert visitors and gives ads somewhere to send people.

Q: Is local SEO different from ads?
A: Yes. Local SEO earns free visibility over time. Ads buy visibility immediately for as long as you pay. Many businesses use both, starting with the profile.


## How to read a monthly marketing report, in plain words
URL: https://themediagraphy.in/guides/how-to-read-a-monthly-marketing-report/
Short answer: A useful report shows how much you spent, how many real enquiries it brought, what each cost, how many calls and direction requests came from Google, what worked, what did not, and what will change next month. If a report is full of impressions and followers but no enquiries, ask for the enquiries first.

### Start with the money
Look first at how much was spent and on what. Ad spend should be shown in your own ad account, and the agency fee should be a separate line. If you cannot see where the money went, ask.

### Then the enquiries
Enquiries are the main number: calls, WhatsApp messages and form submissions. Ask for them split by source, such as Google Maps, Instagram ads, Google ads and your website. The cost of one enquiry is the ad spend divided by the number of enquiries.

### Be careful with vanity numbers
Impressions, reach and followers are not worthless, but they are not customers. A page can gain thousands of followers without a single enquiry. Treat them as supporting information, not as results.

### Google profile numbers
A Google profile report should show views, calls, direction requests and website taps. Trends matter more than one month's number, because seasons move them.

### What worked, what did not
A good report says plainly which posts, ads or offers worked and which did not, and why it thinks so. It should be honest about weak spots, because that is where improvement comes from.

### What changes next month
The most useful part of the report is the plan. It should list a few specific changes with reasons, such as a new offer, a different area, a better photo or a faster reply. Ask your agency to explain each one in plain language.

### Check the follow-up
The report cannot see everything that happens after the enquiry. Compare it with your own record: how many enquiries you got, how many you answered quickly and how many became customers. If the numbers disagree, tell your agency early.

Q: What should be in a monthly report?
A: Spend, enquiries and their cost, calls and direction requests, what worked, what did not and what changes next month, in plain language.

Q: How often should I get a report?
A: Monthly at minimum, with a short call to explain it. Our plans include a monthly report, and a call that ranges from monthly to weekly depending on the plan.

Q: Can I see a sample?
A: Yes. See the sample monthly report on this site, which uses made-up numbers and is clearly labelled as a sample.

Q: Who will I talk to?
A: A real campaign manager from our team, on WhatsApp or call, Monday to Saturday. No bots and no call centre.

Q: What do I need to give you to start?
A: Your business name, logo, phone number, a few photos if you have them and access to your Google and Meta pages. We guide you through each step and it takes about an hour.

Q: Will you create content in Marathi and Hindi?
A: Yes. Posts, reels, ad copy and WhatsApp messages can be in Marathi, Hindi or English, whichever your customers use.

Q: Do you handle Google reviews and my Maps profile?
A: Yes. We set up and verify your Google Business Profile, add photos and offers, and help you collect more genuine reviews with a QR card. We never write fake reviews.

Q: Do you work with businesses outside Kalyan and Dombivli?
A: Yes. We mainly serve Kalyan, Dombivli, Ulhasnagar, Titwala, Ambernath, Badlapur and Thane. We can also run Google and Meta ads for nearby areas.

Q: What if my competitors are also advertising?
A: That is normal in KDMC. We focus on a clear local offer, good photos, fast replies and the right area targeting, so you do not need to outspend them.

Q: What is included in the free audit?
A: You answer about 20 quick questions and tick what you already have in place. You get a score, a category-by-category breakdown, a 30-day plan and the monthly upside you may be missing. It takes about two minutes, needs no sign-up and costs nothing.

Q: What is the free chai and strategy meet?
A: A 30-minute conversation about your numbers, with no sales pitch. We come to your shop for chai, or we can talk on a call or video. The time you pick on our website is a request. We confirm or change it with you on WhatsApp.

Q: What are your working hours?
A: Monday to Saturday, 10 AM to 7 PM IST. Message us on WhatsApp any time and we reply first thing in the next working window.


## Pricing and billing
Q: What does it cost to get started?
A: The audit and the first meeting are free. Plans start at ₹5,999 a month. Your Meta and Google ad spend is separate and paid by you directly to the platforms.

Q: Do you give invoices? Is GST charged?
A: Yes, every payment gets a clear invoice or receipt and a monthly report. We are not registered for GST at present, so the prices shown are what you pay. GST is charged only once our business is registered for it, and when that happens it will be shown as a separate line on your invoice and told to you in advance.

Q: Do you take a commission on ad spend?
A: No. Your ad budget goes straight from your own account to Google and Meta. We never take a cut or add a markup. You pay our plan fee and nothing else.

Q: How much should I spend on ads as a small shop?
A: Start with ₹8,000 to ₹15,000 a month for one shop or clinic. Below ₹5,000 the ads do not get enough data to learn. We will tell you honestly if a smaller budget is better spent on Google Maps and WhatsApp first.

Q: Is the suggested ad spend per post or per reel?
A: No. It is one total monthly budget for all your ads together, paid directly by you to Meta and Google. It is not charged per post or per reel. Your plan fee covers the work of making and managing everything.

Q: Do I have to sign a long contract?
A: No. Plans run month to month. Quarterly and yearly billing only give you a discount. You can stop at any time with notice, and your ad accounts always stay yours.

Q: Can I upgrade or downgrade my plan?
A: Yes. You can move up when you are ready to grow or step down in a slow season. The change applies from your next billing month.

Q: Which plan should I choose?
A: Use our free audit and plan finder. As a rule, Aarambh suits a single shop that wants to be found on Google Maps, Shuru adds content and one Meta campaign, Vikas adds Google and Meta ads management with tracking, and Pragati and Shikhar add landing pages, on-site shoots and automation. We will tell you honestly if a smaller plan fits you better.

Q: How do I pay?
A: By UPI or bank transfer against an invoice, in advance for the month, quarter or year you choose. We do not set up auto-debit or store your card details, and every payment is one you make yourself.


## Results and tracking
Q: How will I know it is working?
A: You get a plain-language report every month and a weekly call. Enquiries are tracked in accounts you own, so you can check every rupee.

Q: Do you guarantee results?
A: No honest agency can promise exact numbers. We promise clear tracking, fast fixes and straight talk about what is and is not working.

Q: How long before I see enquiries?
A: Google Maps improvements usually show in 3 to 6 weeks. Meta lead campaigns can bring the first enquiries within 7 to 14 days, and become steadier by month 2 or 3 after the first optimisation.

Q: What is the difference between a reel and an on-site shoot?
A: A reel is one short vertical video that we edit with captions and local-language text. An on-site shoot is when our team visits your shop, clinic or site and records photos and many clips in one visit, which we then turn into reels, posts and ad creatives.

Q: What is a CRM and do I need one?
A: A CRM is a simple list or app where every enquiry is saved with its status, so no customer is forgotten. Small shops can start with a sheet. Bigger teams get a proper CRM set up in the Shikhar plan.

Q: What is in the monthly report?
A: Leads, cost per lead, calls, what worked, what we changed and what we will do next month, in plain language. You get it on WhatsApp and as a PDF, and we go through it with you on the weekly or fortnightly call your plan includes.


## Google Maps and local SEO
Q: What is a Google Business Profile and why does my shop need one?
A: It is your free listing on Google Search and Maps, with your address, timings, photos, reviews and call and direction buttons. When someone searches "near me", it is often the first thing they see. A complete, active profile is the base of local marketing for any shop, clinic or class.

Q: How do you get a shop into the Google Maps 3-pack?
A: Google says local results depend mainly on relevance, distance and prominence. We set the right categories and services, add real photos, keep your name, address and phone consistent, post regularly, build genuine reviews and add local pages. Nobody can pay for a place or promise a position, and distance is outside anyone's control.

Q: How long does Google Business Profile verification take?
A: Google decides the method, such as a video, phone or email check, and the time it needs. Often it takes a few days, and sometimes longer if Google asks for more proof. We guide you through every step and keep you updated.

Q: Can you remove bad Google reviews?
A: We can flag reviews that break Google's policies, such as spam, fake or off-topic ones, and Google makes the final call. We cannot remove honest negative reviews, and we never write or buy fake reviews. The best answer to a bad review is a polite reply and more genuine happy customers.

Q: How do I get more genuine Google reviews?
A: Ask at the right moment, right after good service. A QR card at the counter and a WhatsApp link make it easy, and replying to every review shows you care. Do not offer gifts or discounts in exchange for 5-star reviews, because that breaks Google's rules and can get reviews removed.

Q: What is local SEO and how is it different from ads?
A: Local SEO earns free, organic visibility in Google Search and Maps for searches near the customer. It takes weeks to build and keeps working. Ads buy visibility straight away for as long as you pay. Most local businesses do best with both, starting with the Google profile because it needs no ad spend.

Q: Do I need a website if I already have a Google Business Profile?
A: You can start without one. A fast mobile page with a WhatsApp button still turns more visitors into enquiries, gives your ads somewhere to send people and lets you show offers and services properly. Many shops begin with the profile and add a page later.


## Instagram, Facebook and Google ads
Q: Should a small local business run Instagram ads or Google ads?
A: It depends on how your customers decide. People who need something now, like a dentist or an AC repair, search on Google. People who buy on impulse or by look, like a salon, restaurant, boutique or gym, respond to Instagram and Facebook. Our audit points you to the right mix, and small budgets often start with one.

Q: What is a Meta lead campaign?
A: It is an ad on Instagram and Facebook that lets people send an enquiry through a short lead form or open a WhatsApp chat with you. The leads arrive in your own account, and we track them from the ad to the enquiry so you can see what each lead costs.

Q: What is click-to-WhatsApp advertising?
A: An ad with a button that opens a WhatsApp chat with your business. It suits India well because many customers prefer to chat. We set up the greeting message and quick replies so every chat starts with the right questions.

Q: What is the Conversions API and why does it matter?
A: It lets your website, form or CRM send enquiry events back to Meta, so tracking stays more reliable when browsers or apps block the usual pixel. Better data helps Meta find similar people. We set up Pixel and Conversions API tracking from the Vikas plan.

Q: Do I control my ad budget?
A: Yes. You set the monthly budget in your own ad account. We recommend how to use it and only spend within the amount you approve in writing. You can see every rupee in your own Ads Manager.

Q: Why are my ads not getting leads?
A: The usual reasons are an unclear offer, the wrong area or radius, weak photos, a slow reply, tracking that is not set up, or an ad that has not finished learning. Our audit checks these one by one, and we fix them in order of impact.

Q: How fast should I reply to an enquiry?
A: Enquiries go cold quickly, so we recommend replying within 15 minutes during working hours. Auto-replies and saved answers on WhatsApp Business help you acknowledge at once, and then you follow up personally.

Q: Can you advertise a clinic, coaching class or real estate project?
A: Yes, within the rules. Medical practice, real estate and education advertising have strict rules, for example on claims and on showing a MahaRERA registration number. We keep ads factual and tell you if a claim looks risky. You remain responsible for your licences and for proving your claims.


## Websites, landing pages and WhatsApp
Q: What is a landing page and when do I need one?
A: A landing page is one focused page for a single offer, such as a free trial class or a check-up, with a clear WhatsApp button or form. When ads send people there instead of a busy home page, more of them take action. It is included from the Pragati plan.

Q: Why does my website need to be fast on mobile?
A: Most local customers browse on a phone, often on 4G and in a hurry. A slow page loses them before they see your offer. We build light, mobile-first pages with a WhatsApp button on every page.

Q: Who owns my website, domain and content?
A: You do. The domain and ad accounts are in your name, the content we create is assigned to you once fees are paid, and we hand over access if you leave. Our own templates and tools stay ours.

Q: What is WhatsApp lead routing?
A: It sends each enquiry from your ads, website and Google profile to the right person on your team on WhatsApp, with auto-replies, labels, catalogue and away messages. It means no enquiry sits unanswered in one person's phone.

Q: Do you use the WhatsApp Business app or the API?
A: Most small shops start with the free WhatsApp Business app, with its catalogue, quick replies and labels. Bigger teams may move to the WhatsApp Business API with a CRM, which we set up in the Shikhar plan. Meta charges for some API messages, and you pay that to Meta directly.

Q: Can you send WhatsApp broadcasts to my customers?
A: Only to people who have agreed to hear from you, and following WhatsApp's own rules. We do not buy or use bought contact lists, and every broadcast must let people opt out.


## Content, reels and shoots
Q: What does an on-site shoot include?
A: Our team visits your shop, clinic or site, records photos and many clips in one visit, and then turns them into reels, posts and ad creatives. The Pragati plan includes one shoot a month and the Shikhar plan includes two.

Q: Do you shoot outside Kalyan?
A: We come to Kalyan, Dombivli, Ulhasnagar, Titwala and nearby areas as part of our normal visits. For places further away, we agree the plan and any travel cost with you first, and show it on the invoice.

Q: Can I use my own photos and videos?
A: Yes. Send them on WhatsApp or by a shared folder and we edit them into posts and reels. Please make sure you own the rights to them and to any person or music in them.

Q: Do you use stock or AI-made images for my business?
A: We prefer real pictures of your real shop, because local customers can tell the difference. If we ever use a stock or AI-made image for a background or a festive creative, we tell you, and we never pass it off as your real premises.

Q: How often should I post on Instagram?
A: Steady beats frequent. A realistic rhythm you can keep up works better than bursts. Our plans start at 8 posts a month and go up to 12 posts plus 4 reels a month, and we plan them around your offers and local festivals.

Q: Where is the mediagraphy.in based?
A: We are based in Kalyan East, Maharashtra, and we serve businesses across Kalyan, Dombivli, Ulhasnagar, Titwala, Ambernath, Badlapur and Thane. We can meet at your shop or talk on a call or video, Monday to Saturday, 10 AM to 7 PM.

Q: Do you work in Kalyan West, Dombivli and Ulhasnagar?
A: Yes. We work with shops, clinics, classes and builders on both sides of the Kalyan station, in Dombivli East and West, in Ulhasnagar camps and along the Kalyan-Shil and Badlapur roads. Pick the area page that matches yours to see how we help there.

Q: Do you work with businesses outside the KDMC area?
A: Yes. Google Maps work and Google and Meta ads can run for nearby cities, and we can work online with you wherever you are. For visits and shoots far from Kalyan, we agree the plan and any travel cost with you first.

Q: Why choose a local agency in Kalyan?
A: We know the roads, the festivals, the language people use and what customers in KDMC respond to, and we can walk into your shop. That does not mean guaranteed results, and we say so. It means advice that fits your area and quick, in-person help.


## Privacy, security and your contract
Q: Is your website safe to use? Do you track me?
A: The site loads only over HTTPS, runs no cookies, analytics or third-party scripts, and uses a strict security policy so it cannot load code from elsewhere. The tools calculate inside your browser. Data leaves your device only when you tap a send or book button.

Q: How do you protect my business and customer data?
A: We collect the minimum, limit access to the three founders with two-step verification, keep the enquiry log private, use role-based access to your ad accounts and never ask for passwords or OTPs. If something goes wrong we tell you quickly and report as the law requires. Details are in our Privacy Policy.

Q: Do you follow India's data protection law?
A: Yes. India's Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 and its 2025 Rules were notified on 13 November 2025, and most duties for businesses start on 13 May 2027. We already follow them: a clear notice, consent, minimum data, deletion on request, a grievance contact and breach reporting.

Q: Is there a written contract?
A: Yes. Before any paid plan begins, we share a Service Agreement and an order form with your plan, fees and start date. It is month to month with no lock-in, and nothing is charged until you have read and accepted it. Read the standard terms on our Service Agreement page.

Q: Who owns my ad accounts, content and customer data?
A: You do. Ad accounts, pages and your customers' data stay in your name, the content we make for you is assigned to you once fees are paid, and we only use customer data to deliver your service.

Q: What happens to my data if I stop working with you?
A: We hand over access and files within 7 days of your request, send a final report and remove our own access. We return or delete your customers' data within 30 days after the agreement ends, unless the law requires us to keep it.

Q: What is your refund and cancellation policy?
A: You can cancel any time, with no lock-in or penalty. A month that has started is not refunded, a month we failed to deliver is credited or refunded, and early exit from a quarterly or yearly plan is settled at the monthly rate. Refunds go back within 7 working days. See the full Refund and Cancellation Policy.

Q: Are you a registered company?
A: We are a small independent studio run by three founders, and we are not registered as a company, LLP or firm at present. Contracts are made with the founders together, and we will tell you in writing if that changes. We are also not registered for GST at present.

Q: How do I report a security problem or make a complaint?
A: Write to growth@themediagraphy.in or message us on WhatsApp. For a security issue, share it privately, access only what you need to show it, and give us time to fix it. For a data or service complaint, we acknowledge within 2 working days and aim to resolve it within 30 days.
